intended_object: The canonical invertible 2-cell eqToHom(e₁·e₂) ≅ eqToHom e₁ ≫ eqToHom e₂ in a bicategory for equalities of objects e₁ : x = y, e₂ : y = z. When both are reflexivity, it reduces to the coherence isomorphism 𝟙ₓ ≅ 𝟙ₓ ≫ 𝟙ₓ, the inverse left unitor. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body substitutes along both equalities, reducing to the case x = y = z with both equalities rfl. There it uses (λ_ (𝟙 x)).symm, the canonical coherence 2-isomorphism 𝟙 x ≅ 𝟙 x ≫ 𝟙 x. Since equalities of objects reduce to rfl, this determines the 2-cell completely. Using the inverse right unitor instead would make no difference, because λ_{𝟙} = ρ_{𝟙} by bicategorical coherence. The definition matches its docstring and the lemmas in the same file: the refl/refl case gives (λ_ (𝟙 x)).symm, the refl-right case gives (ρ_ (eqToHom e₁)).symm, the refl-left case gives (λ_ (eqToHom e₁)).symm, and the associator compatibility lemmas also agree. It is stated for an arbitrary bicategory, its natural generality. I found no other Mathlib declaration providing this isomorphism. One could argue that eqToHom is a type-theoretic device, but the construction is a genuine canonical coherence isomorphism and is defined correctly.
